title: Sequential, mixed or staged: what the order of training does to the families
purpose: Train the same 120 steps (at 3e-6, three times the rate of the matrix, so that the weights move far enough for forgetting to show) three ways: one family group after another, everything mixed, and a mixed base followed by a focus stage and a short refresh. After every stage score every family, so forgetting shows up as a drop in a family the stage did not train.

checks.description: all nine stage runs completed and each later stage started from the weights of the stage before
checks.because: The stages of a chain are separate runs: each saves its final weights to the bucket and the next starts from them, so the chain is auditable run by run.

checks.description: sequential training forgets: after the last stage at least one family trained earlier is at least 0.05 below its own best score of the chain
checks.because: Each stage trains only its own families, so nothing holds the earlier families in place while the weights move; whatever they shared with the new stage is overwritten.

checks.description: a focus stage keeps its neighbours: in the staged run, the families the focus stage barely trained lost less than the sequential run's worst loss
checks.because: The focus stage is 70% instruction and tools and 30% the other four families, so the others keep receiving gradient while the focus families improve.

checks.description: the three orders are compared on the same footing: 120 optimizer steps each, the same model and the same held-out sets
checks.because: The steps are 24 x 5, 60 + 30 + 30 and 120; the comparison is of order, not of compute.

notes: After 120 steps (mean over the six families / worst family): sequential 0.744 / 0.237, staged with refresh 0.870 / 0.532, mixed 0.869 / 0.530. One seed per order: differences of a few points are inside the noise of S03.
